title: The Father of Rabbi Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A baraita reciter in Rabbi Zeira’s time. [Gittin 85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.85a.4) has him reciting before Rabbi Zeira. He is always called “the father of Rabbi Avin recited”: [Yoma 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.29a.9), [Gittin 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.53a.8), [Bava Kamma 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.117a.5), [Sanhedrin 76a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.76a.17) and [Niddah 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.37a.11). [Sanhedrin 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.51b.20) has “the father of Shmuel bar Avin recited”; Hyman proposes “the father of Rabbi Avin,” as in Dikdukei Soferim.[^3]

notes.text: Tanna here describes a reciter of baraitot in Zeira’s academy. The alternatives concern the father of Avin versus the father of Shmuel bar Avin.
The consulted Sanhedrin 51b text reads the father of Shmuel bar Avin; the father-of-Rabbi-Avin correction in Dikdukei Soferim remains Hyman’s edition report.

The linked passages use “the father of Rabbi Avin recited”; Gittin 85a adds that he recited before Rabbi Zeira. The longer name in Sanhedrin 51b is a separate reading which Hyman proposes to shorten. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3061&lang=en).
